newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs rally to higher end on bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs rally to higher end on bargain hunting.

text.p: Bargain hunting by domestic institutions and foreign investors led the market's rally by Friday's close, brokers said.

The composite stock index rose 2.18 percent, or 16.72 points, to a provisional close of 782.88. Advancing shares overwhelmed decliners 701 to 134 with 120 stocks going limit up. Volume also improved, reaching 20.07 million.
"The mood has considerably lightened," said a Schroders Securities broker. "Quite a large number of shares went limit up, basically due to a technical rebound and bargain hunting."
The index has fallen 20 percent since the end of April.
But brokers said the market's rise would be hard to sustain past the 800 level because economic fundamentals and the supply and demand situation have not changed.

Rumours that the scheduled announcement on government plans to raise the foreign shareholders' ceiling was imminent underpinned the buying interest. The government has said it plans to raise the limit to 20 percent from the current 18 percent by the end of the year.
A stabilised three-year corporate bond yields added to the feel-good factor.
The yields fell for the past two days, and bond dealers said the yields declined to 12.18 percent during Friday's trading.
The prospect of margin trading in second tier shares from September, and employee securities savings plans in October were also seen bringing more funds to the market, brokers said.
Blue chips that had lagged recently were in the spotlight. Samsung Electronics gained 2,600 won to 638,000, while Dacom rose 7,000 won to 129,500.
Financial, construction and trading stocks, known collectively as "troika" shares, regained investor favour.
The index was later revised to 782.87, up 16.71
